record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: What are the temperature, parton-type, parton-energy, and path-length dependences of the jet-quenching stopping power q-hat divided by T cubed, and why do spectral slopes, fragmentation functions, and energy-loss coefficients appear to cancel so that the nuclear-modification factor RAA has nearly invariant magnitude and shape across parton flavours and collision energies?

evidence.quote: The "stopping power of sQGP", q̂/T3, is now known to about 30% and the predicted mass dependence has been investigated with heavy flavour mesons.

Future high precision measurements with more statistics, in particular in the golden γ-jet channel, and new detectors (sPHENIX), are needed to confirm the ever so slight hint of a non-trivial temperature dependence of the stopping power (RHIC → LHC) and nail its parton type, parton energy, and path-length dependence.

And finally, somewhat unsettling remains, at least to this author, the miraculous cancellations required concurrently in spectral slopes, fragmentation functions, and energy loss coefficients, in order to explain the nearly invariant magnitude and shape of RAA for different parton flavours (g ≈ u/d/s ≈ c ≈ b ≈ J/ψ) and at different energies (0.2 ≈ 2.8 ≈ 5 TeV).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, a strongly coupled quark–gluon plasma (sQGP) is produced with a local temperature T. A high-energy parton (gluon g, light quark u/d/s, charm c, or bottom b) traversing this medium loses energy via interactions characterized by the jet transport coefficient q̂, defined as the mean squared transverse momentum acquired per unit path length. The dimensionless ratio q̂/T^3 is regarded as the medium's stopping power. The nuclear modification factor R_AA(p_T) for a given hadron species is defined as the ratio of the yield in nucleus–nucleus collisions to the yield in proton–proton collisions scaled by the average number of binary nucleon–nucleon collisions, as a function of transverse momentum p_T.

Problem. Determine, from first principles in a controlled QCD-based framework of in-medium parton energy loss:

(a) the functional dependence of q̂/T^3 on the medium temperature T, on the parton flavour (mass), on the parton energy E, and on the in-medium path length L; and

(b) provide a quantitative explanation of why the convolution of (i) the partonic spectral slopes of the initial hard scattering, (ii) the vacuum and medium-modified fragmentation functions, and (iii) the energy-loss kernel produces an R_AA whose magnitude and p_T-shape are nearly invariant across parton flavours (g, u/d/s, c, b, and J/ψ) and across collision energies spanning roughly 0.2, 2.76, and 5 TeV per nucleon pair. In particular, identify the cancellation mechanism (or rule it out) that makes R_AA approximately universal despite the strong dependence of each individual ingredient on flavour and energy.
artifact.status_search_result: The temperature, parton-type, energy, and path-length dependences of q̂/T^3 remain active areas of investigation. The JETSCAPE Collaboration's Bayesian extractions (2021–2024) have constrained q̂/T^3 to roughly 30–50% precision and reported mild T- and E-dependence, but the parton-type and path-length dependences and the universality of R_AA remain not fully understood. The problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: JETSCAPE Bayesian inference of q-hat
status_evidence.snippet: Multistage Monte Carlo simulation constrains q̂/T^3 with significant uncertainty across temperature ranges.
status_evidence.claim: q̂/T^3 is constrained but its temperature and energy dependence are still being mapped out.

status_evidence.title: sPHENIX and jet quenching prospects
status_evidence.snippet: sPHENIX aims to measure jet observables to nail down the temperature, energy, and path-length dependence of jet quenching.
status_evidence.claim: Future measurements are still needed, indicating the question remains open.
